title: 2013 AMC 12B Problem 22
statement:
Let \(m \gt 1\) and \(n \gt 1\) be integers. Suppose that the product of the solutions for \(x\) of the equation

\[ \begin{aligned} &8(\log_n x)(\log_m x) - 7\log_n x \\ &\quad {}- 6\log_m x - 2013 = 0 \end{aligned} \]

is the smallest possible integer. What is \(m + n?\)

solutions.text: Writing \(\log_n x = \tfrac{\log x}{\log n}\) and \(\log_m x = \tfrac{\log x}{\log m},\) the equation becomes a quadratic in \(\log x\) whose roots sum to \(\log(x_1 x_2)\) \(= \tfrac18(7\log m + 6\log n).\) Hence \(N^8=m^7n^6,\) where \(N=x_1x_2.\) For each prime dividing \(mn,\) let its exponents in \(m,n\) be \(a,b.\) Then \(7a+6b\equiv0\pmod8.\) An odd \(a\) is impossible. If \(a=0,\) then \(b\) is a multiple of \(4\) and this prime contributes at least \(p^3,\) but some other prime must divide \(m.\) If \(a\equiv0\pmod8\) is positive, its contribution to \(N\) is at least \(p^7;\) if \(a\equiv2\pmod8,\) then \(b\equiv3\pmod4\) and the least contribution is \(p^4.\) Every other positive even \(a\) gives more. Thus the minimum uses only \(p=2\) with \((a,b)=(2,3),\) giving \(N=16,\) \(m=4,\) and \(n=8.\) So \(m+n=12.\) Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: Use \(\log_n x = \dfrac{\log x}{\log n}\) to turn the equation into a quadratic in \(\log x\)
The product of the roots satisfies \(\log(x_1 x_2)\) \(= \tfrac18(7\log m + 6\log n),\) so \((x_1 x_2)^8 = m^7 n^6;\) minimize this integer
